title: One minus shift is monic on the sequential coproduct
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $E:\mathbf N\to\operatorname{Comp}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ a sequential system of cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Put $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}E_n$ and let $\iota_n:E_n\to A$ be the coproduct injections. The morphism $u:A\to A$ determined by $u\iota_n=\iota_n-\iota_{n+1}E(n\leq n+1)$ is a monomorphism. No injectivity of the transition morphisms is assumed.

source.place: Tag 093W (lemma-colim-sequence), proof by finite initial-sum short exact sequences; used in Tag 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim)

proof.text: In every degree form A_n = the sum of E_j for j < n and B_n = the sum of E_j for j ≤ n. Define u_n by ι_j minus the transition to summand j+1. Project onto the first n summands. The composite is 1 minus a nilpotent lower triangular shift, with inverse the finite geometric sum. Thus u_n is split monic, including n=0. The u_n commute with inclusions of initial sums.

Sheaves of modules form a Grothendieck abelian category, so the sequential colimit of these monomorphisms is monic. The two colimits of finite initial sums are the coproduct of all terms: maps out of either colimit are exactly compatible maps out of finite sums, hence families of maps out of all summands. Checking each coproduct injection identifies the colimit map with 1-shift. Evaluation computes coproducts degreewise, so the map is monic in each cochain degree and hence in the category of complexes.
